notes: Background: RelayWorks builds mid-market contact center SaaS used by retailers and telcos. Heavy focus on automating refunds and escalations via connectors to legacy ticketing systems.
Current stack: homegrown ticketing + Zendesk for overflow; orchestration layer exposes REST hooks to agents UI.

Primary ask: reliable tool-calling to support systems for create/update tickets, issue refunds via payment gateway, escalate to Tier 2 with attachments + context. Must record audit trail for each action.
Latency/throughput: agent UI expects <200ms perceived latency for action confirmation; batch ticket updates during spikes (Black Friday) => bursts to 3k TPS across tenancy (prefers autoscaling).

Reliability: need automatic retry with idempotency keys, exactly-once semantics for refunds (payments), circuit-breaker fallback to human queue if downstream fails, and graceful degradation (summaries only) during downtime.
Security/compliance: no PII persisted in Redwood logs; KMS for keys, audit logs surfaced to their SIEM, data residency requirement for EU customers (must stay in eu region).
Quote from CTO on 2026-02-14 call: "We can’t accept double refunds — transactional guarantees are non-negotiable. Also need clear trace from agent action -> ticket id -> payment trace."

Integration notes: need pre-built connector for their legacy ticketing API (token-based, 2 endpoints: /tickets, /tickets/batch) OR a robust tool-calling SDK we can host in VPC. Idempotency via X-Idempotency-Key header.
Risk: current POC failed on race condition when two agents update same ticket; SRE wants request-level locking or optimistic concurrency tokens.
Commercial: leaning toward Dedicated reserved capacity if performance during spikes is validated; Private if contract/legal require on-prem for certain retail customers.
Demo feedback: agents liked auto-summarize + suggested actions but worried about occasional hallucinated suggested refunds (false positives). Need strong guardrails + policy rules.
Next immediate actions: Redwood to provide architecture diagram for tool-calling flow, sample idempotent refund implementation, and cost estimate for dedicated pool sized for 5k TPS bursts.
